This method connects 1D visualization views with 3D volume rendering by using Hilbert space-filling curve codes to define selection ranges [S1].

The claim states that the method connects 1D visualization views with 3D volume rendering using Hilbert space-filling curve codes to define selection ranges. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in Section 3.5 'Brushing and Linking', stating: 'We connect the DVL and 3D views using brushing and linking... We use the ROIs’ first and last Hilbert codes as selection ranges for that.' It further explains that selecting ROIs in the 1D plot highlights corresponding cells in the 3D view using these codes. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

- **Time Complexity:** The containment test uses direct integer comparisons on Hilbert codes [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the selection ranges for highlighting cells (the containment test) are defined by the ROIs' first and last Hilbert codes. It further explains that the test involves transforming the center of the cell being sampled to Hilbert space to test it against these ROIs. Since Hilbert codes are integers, testing if a sampled point's code falls within a range defined by two other codes (first and last) constitutes direct integer comparisons.

This aligns with the claim's description of mapping to a 1D range of Hilbert codes instead of a 3D bounding box (or list of cells) for compact representation.

The technique builds on the concept of Dynamic Volume Lines (DVL) and extends it to support 3D view interaction through Hilbert space-filling curves [S1].

The evidence supports the claim that the technique connects 1D and 3D views using Hilbert space-filling curves (Hilbert codes) and involves 'brushing and linking' to highlight cells in the 3D view based on selections in the 1D plot. However, the evidence does not explicitly state that the technique 'builds on the concept of Dynamic Volume Lines (DVL)' in the sense of extending the DVL concept itself. Instead, it states that the authors implement 'interactive volume lines (IVLs)' which are described as 'the GPU-accelerated version of dynamic volume lines,' and that they 'connect the DVL and 3D views.' While IVLs are related to DVL, the specific phrasing 'extends [DVL] to support 3D view interaction' is not directly supported; rather, the text describes a new technique (IVL) that connects existing DVL functionality to 3D views. Furthermore, the claim implies a direct extension of the DVL concept, whereas the text presents IVL as a distinct implementation (GPU-accelerated) that facilitates the connection. Therefore, while the core mechanism (Hilbert codes for 3D interaction) is supported, the specific relationship to DVL as an 'extension' of the concept is not fully supported by the provided text, which frames it as a new implementation (IVL) that links to DVL.
